issue.title: Status of testing Providers that were prepared on April 21, 2026
issue.body:
### Body

I have a kind request for all the contributors to the latest provider distributions release.
Could you please help us to test the RC versions of the providers?

The guidelines on how to test providers can be found in

[Verify providers by contributors](https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/main/dev/README_RELEASE_PROVIDERS.md#verify-the-release-candidate-by-contributors)

Let us know in the comments, whether the issue is addressed.

These are providers that require testing as there were some substantial changes introduced:

comments.body: @radu-gheorghe  @thomasht86 - please make sure that Vespa provider is ready :)
Hi, I've tested my part of the change (#65170), and it looks good :)

I tested my fix (#65579) for the OpenLineage provider the safe_getattr logic is working as expected and handles the DetachedInstanceError when accessing note or deadlines on detached objects this should stop the listener crashes we were seeing in Airflow 3.2+. Looks good for the 2.15.0rc1 release!

Hi. Thanks for the nudge!

Since it's the first time I do this, allow me to be verbose :) 

I've started Airflow like so:
```
breeze start-airflow --use-airflow-version 3.2.0 --python 3.12 --backend postgres \
    --load-example-dags --load-default-connections
```

Then installed the Vespa provider in it:
```
pip install apache-airflow-providers-vespa==0.1.0rc1
```

Then restarted everything, logged into the UI, created a Vespa connection that pointed to a local Vespa, ran the example DAG (which is a reasonable smoke test for everything), worked.

Is this OK, or should I do other things as well? Like the sftp and ssh providers which are touched by my PR?

Google provider is tested and working good
**+1 for Google**
Tested all my contributions, looks good!
Tested #65299 against 9.26.0rc1, AWS China regex works as expected. +1.
Tested #65540 and the migration finally works now.

Tested Celery 3.19.0rc1,  task are failing on airflow 3.2.0 with `ImportError: cannot import name 'ExecutorWorkload' from 'airflow.executors.workloads'` at celery_executor_utils.py:213. Both `ExecutorWorkload` and `BaseExecutor.run_workload` only exist on main (3.3+),  but the gate is `AIRFLOW_V_3_2_PLUS`, regression from #62645. Fix in #65752.  

cc: @ferruzzi  @shahar1

I have tested and verified Amazon Provider (9.26.0rc1).

- Checks: Signature, Checksum, and RAT check passed.
- Functional Test: Successfully installed and ran example DAGs in Breeze (Python 3.13).
- Compatibility: Confirmed it works fine in Python 3.13 as requested in the issue.

Thanks!

> Is this OK, or should I do other things as well? Like the sftp and ssh providers which are touched by my PR?

All good there :)

> Tested Celery 3.19.0rc1,  task are failing on airflow 3.2.0 with `ImportError: cannot import name 'ExecutorWorkload' from 'airflow.executors.workloads'` at celery_executor_utils.py:213. Both `ExecutorWorkload` and `BaseExecutor.run_workload` only exist on main (3.3+),  but the gate is `AIRFLOW_V_3_2_PLUS`, regression from #62645. Fix in #65752.  
> 
> cc: @ferruzzi  @shahar1  

Thanks! Excluding celery from this release, RC2 will include the patch.

Shortly after #65395 and #65396 were merged, it was pointed out that there could be a potential security concern where a caller without team context could access the team variables/connections. I opened a PR (#65703) to address those issues.

Hi,
Since RC2 also completed, can we close this one as well?
